deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): X is a topological space and Y ⊂ X a 'non-singular' subspace, i.e. a topological manifold. X is 'equisingular along Y' at y if some neighbourhood U of y satisfies U ≅ N × Y_U for a pointed space (N,a), with Y_U corresponding to {a} × Y_U. A point x is ν-mobile if some such Y through x has dim_x Y ≥ ν. Its mobility order ν(x) is the largest such ν; it exists when X is locally finite-dimensional. Equivalently, ν(x) is the largest k such that the germ (X,x) is homeomorphic to (N,a) × (R^k,0).

This page:
(1) Mob^i(X) is the set of i-mobile points. This gives a decreasing chain X = Mob^0 ⊃ Mob^1 ⊃ Mob^2 ⊃ …, whose intersection is empty iff ν(x) is defined everywhere. The complements F_i(X) = X − Mob^{i+1}(X) form an increasing chain F_0 ⊂ F_1 ⊂ …, with union X under the same condition.
- F_i is the set of points of mobility ≤ i; F_0 is the set of immobile ('elementary') singularities.
- Grothendieck first wrote and then struck out 'fermé' for Mob^i. That is right: i-mobility is an open condition. If U ≅ N × Y_U, every point (n,y) lies on the slice {n} × Y_U, along which X is again locally a product. So Mob^i is open, ν is lower semicontinuous, and the F_i form a closed filtration.
(2) For a fixed X he asks whether three statements hold. Set Y_i = F_i − F_{i−1} = ν^{-1}(i), with F_{−1} = ∅.
- Prop A: each Y_i is a topological manifold of pure dimension i, and X is equisingular along Y_i. Spaces satisfying A are named 'presque raisonnables'.
- Prop B: near each point of Y_i, (X,Y_i) ≅ Y_i × (N,o) with o an immobile point of N. The local homeomorphism type of (N,o) depends only on the connected component of Y_i. The margin asks whether B holds for every 'dévissable' space; the next page says B follows from A.
- Prop C: (Y_i)_x is the largest germ of submanifold through x along which X is equisingular. All other such germs correspond 1–1 to germs of (locally flat) submanifolds of Y_i.
(3) In modern terms this is the intrinsic (coarsest, canonical) topological stratification of a space: strata are level sets of the 'local Euclidean factor dimension'. A asks when this intrinsic filtration is a genuine stratification. B gives local triviality with a well-defined normal slice. C gives maximality of strata.
(4) Purpose: within the 1974 'topologie modérée' programme, these are the axioms a class of tame spaces (presumably 'dévissable' ones) should satisfy so that every space carries a canonical stratification. This is a precursor to the stratified-structure discussions in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: Prop A as written says the strata Y_i have 'codim. i'. By definition, points of mobility i lie on i-dimensional manifolds, so the correct statement is dimension i, not codimension i (unless the indexing was meant to change, which is not done consistently).

Prop A is false for general locally finite-dimensional spaces. For X = Cantor set × R, every point has mobility 1, so Y_1 = X, which is not a 1-manifold. Grothendieck recognises this by restricting to 'presque raisonnables' spaces.

In the topological category, the uniqueness claim in Prop B (local type of the slice (N,o) constant on components) and the implicit additivity ν(N × R^i) = ν(N) + i (stated as Prop D on the next page) both fail. Double suspension theorem (Edwards, Cannon, late 1970s): for a non-simply-connected homology 3-sphere Σ, c(Σ) × R^2 = c(S^1 * Σ) ≅ R^6. So the cone point, immobile in c(Σ), gives points of mobility 6 rather than 2. A decomposition N × R^i with N immobile at o therefore does not determine the stratum, and slices are not unique.

Further cancellation phenomena (N_1 × R^k ≅ N_2 × R^k with non-homeomorphic germs) mean normal slices are generally defined only up to such stabilisation. This is unsure in exact generality, but it is known that links of intrinsic strata of topological pseudomanifolds are not homeomorphism invariants.
Prop C's 1–1 correspondence needs 'régulières' to mean locally flat. Wild submanifolds of Y_i need not give local product structures.

ideas.what: Mobility index ν(x): the largest dimension of a Euclidean factor splitting off the germ (X,x); immobile points are those with ν = 0. Lower semicontinuity of ν, so the F_i form a closed filtration.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Akin (PL intrinsic dimension, 1969); Siebenmann (CS sets, 1972); King (topological intrinsic filtration, 1985); see Friedman's book on intersection homology

ideas.what: Prop A/B: asking when the intrinsic filtration is a locally trivial stratification with constant normal slice; class of 'presque raisonnables' spaces.
ideas.modern_name: intrinsic stratification of CS sets / pseudomanifolds; locally cone-like (Siebenmann) stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Siebenmann; King; Goresky–MacPherson (topological invariance of intersection homology)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses tame topology and stratified structures in general terms, not this definition

ideas.what: Prop C: maximality of strata — every submanifold germ of equisingularity lies in the stratum, and such germs correspond to submanifold germs of the stratum.
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in stratification theory (Mather, Teissier for canonical Whitney stratifications)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axioms (A: intrinsic strata are manifolds; B: local product structure with immobile, component-constant slice; D: additivity of mobility) form a precise test list for a 'tame topology'. They fail in general topology exactly because of the later Edwards–Cannon double suspension phenomena (c(Σ) × R^2 ≅ R^6). This makes a concrete, previously unremarked link between his motivation for topologie modérée and the decomposition-space results of the late 1970s. In o-minimal or PL settings the intrinsic stratification behaves as he wants.
missed.quote: Appelons "presque raisonnables" les espaces de dim. finie loc. pour lesquels Prop A soit vraie.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The axioms give an intrinsic, topology-only criterion for a 'tame' class (e.g. the open question of which classes are 'dévissable') that could be compared with o-minimal and definable-stratification frameworks.

missed.claim: The question whether every 'dévissable' space satisfies Prop B (and A), i.e. has a canonical intrinsic stratification with locally constant normal slices, is left open.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. For definable sets in o-minimal structures, analogous statements are known in the definable category, but a purely topological characterisation is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page defines what is essentially the topological intrinsic filtration (later standard via King 1985, with PL antecedents by Akin), notes correctly that it is an open/closed filtration, and asks the right stratification questions. This is a nice unpublished 1974 formulation, but the ideas are now well known. The implicit additivity and slice-uniqueness assumptions fail topologically in a way Grothendieck could not have known in 1974.

The struck-out word replacing 'fermé' is consistent with Mob^i being open.

Margin of Prop B: 'décidable' should be 'dévissable' (the word is struck and rewritten as 'dévissable?').
Prop A: 'v^{-1}' is ν^{-1}, i.e. the mobility index ν.
